flags.statement: Messrs. Schiller's and Dewey's theories have suffered a hailstorm…
flags.reason: the quotes are split at "Messrs." and "Schiller's and Dewey's theories…" and join into one sentence. The content is supported, but the joining is awkward.

flags.statement: A hailstorm of contempt and ridicule throws so much sidelight…
flags.reason: the author-name span "William James" is inserted mid-clause, and the footnote 4 quote is a subject lifted from the earlier sentence. The source subject of "throws" is "I should not mention this, but for the fact that it throws…", where "it" is the fact of the treatment. The statement makes the hailstorm itself the subject, which is close but loosely reworded. Grade: reworded.

flags.statement: …to which I, William James, have opposed…
flags.reason: the author span "William James" is inserted into the quote "to which I have opposed". The note otherwise never names the author, so this one is arguably needed, but the footnote points to the frontmatter or title rather than a quote of the author's name. Whether a cut of "I" works is debatable; "I" would otherwise dangle, so the name span is plausible. Grade: pass for the span, with a note that the source does not use "William James" in the lecture text, only in the frontmatter title.

flags.statement: Such truths are not real truth.
flags.reason: "Such truths" refers to the "article of truth" in the previous statement, which is resolvable. Pass on that point. However, "Such tests are merely subjective." and "As against this…" depend on the previous statements and also resolve. No fault.

flags.statement: He accuses us, Messrs. Dewey, Schiller and their allies, of DENYING truth…
flags.reason: "He" is the rationalist from the previous statement (resolves). "us" is spliced with an outside-section name span to mean Dewey and Schiller. In the source, "us" is James speaking as a pragmatist; the splice narrows it to Dewey and Schiller and their allies, which changes the referent (reworded). The span itself names a source phrase from the Theory of Truth section ("Messrs. Dewey, Schiller and their allies"), which refers to the right people there, but James's "us" includes himself. Grade: wrong referent, since the statement then also makes "whereas we have only sought…" mean those same people.

flags.statement: Pragmatism only follows here the example of the sister-sciences…
flags.reason: the source subject is "It" (pragmatism, per the previous sentence "the pragmatism which they advocate"), so replacing "It" with "Pragmatism" is a fair repair. The cut dropped "I hope that as these lectures go on… may be what approves itself to you…", which is stance, so fine. Pass.

flags.statement: It converts the absolutely empty notion…
flags.reason: the quote is split mid-sentence at "'correspondence'" and "between our minds and reality". The parenthetical "(what that may mean we must ask later)" is dropped, which is stance, so no loss. Pass.
